title.narrative: Strengthening disability inclusion through the UNESCO Strategy

description.narrative: UNESCO adopted its Disability Inclusion Strategy (2026-2029) at the 43rd General Conference, reaffirming its commitment to ensuring that persons with disabilities are fully included across all its fields of competence — education, sciences, culture and communication. The Strategy is organized around three mutually reinforcing pillars to ensure disability inclusion around UNESCO’s programmes, policies and operations: Pillar 1: Strengthening Organizational Capacity for Disability Inclusion; Pillar 2: Enhancing Disability Inclusion in Programmatic Work, and Pillar 3: Mainstreaming and Consolidating Disability Inclusion. As part of the Strategy, the work of the Intersectoral Task Team on Disability and Rights (ITT) will be reinforced, ensuring that strategic development, implementation and monitoring of programmes and initiatives will be optimized across Sectors and Field Offices. Moreover, the Strategy will be complemented by a targeted Action Plan that will leverage the available knowledge, expertise, networks and resources that UNESCO has at its disposal. ﻿As part of Pillar 3 of the UNESCO Disability Inclusion Strategy, the Disability Inclusion Global Knowledge Hub is envisioned as a dynamic, multi-functional platform dedicated to advancing disability inclusion through knowledge generation, exchange and capacity development. Its core purpose is to support Member States and stakeholders in translating international commitments, including the CRPD, into effective policies and practices.
